kypExtensions.summary: The two-question reading of the printed test-selection algorithm: FIRST the outcome's scale (Variables to be compared → Numerical (means) vs Categorical (proportions) — means language goes left, percentage/proportion language goes right), THEN the second dial (means branch → COUNT THE GROUPS: 2 → t-test, ≥ 3 → ANOVA; proportions branch → GAUGE THE SAMPLE: Small → Fisher's exact test, Large → Chi-square test), landing on exactly one of the four leaves — plus the geometry observation that each leaf box prints DIRECTLY below its criterion, so the tree's layout itself encodes the routing.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the tree's boxes and labels but never states the ordered protocol (scale first, dial second) nor names the dials; the two-question synthesis is KYP's.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms[0] test-selection-tree + blocks[3] the steps block + the registry visual's Zone A route chips and rule strip

kypExtensions.summary: The means-family vs proportions-family engine: why a measured, averaged outcome (mean blood pressure) belongs to t-test/ANOVA while a counted, categorical outcome (the proportion with essential hypertension) belongs to chi-square/Fisher — anchored on the printed fence '(not mean values)' in the chi-square cell, the printed pairing of the two 3-group examples (3 ethnic groups by MEANS → ANOVA vs 3 age groups by PROPORTIONS → chi-square: same group count, different branch), and the observation that chi-square handles 2 OR MORE proportions while Fisher's scope is exactly 2.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the four Checks cells and the four examples but never connects them as one 2-axis design space (outcome scale × second dial); the family engine and the paired-example drill are KYP's organization.
kypExtensions.location: core.why + mechanisms[1] outcome-scale-engine + blocks[2] the decoder list + usmle.traps[1] and traps[3]

kypExtensions.summary: The small-sample switch: within the proportions family, the print swaps the leaf by sample size — Fisher's exact test is used 'instead of chi-square test with small samples' (its scope exactly 2 percentages or proportions of categorical, nominal outcomes; the printed example's 20 men and 20 women is the print's own illustration of small) — with the documented absence of a mnemonic in the Fisher row (no mnemonic invented), and the KYP-context note that the print names no numeric threshold for 'small' (the usual expected-cell-count worry is flagged as unprinted context, never a correction).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the substitution sentence and the 20+20 example but never frames sample size as the branch's dial nor documents the mnemonic absence; the switch layer and the threshold caveat are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea MOVE 2 + blocks[4] the compare block + usmle.pivots[2] + the registry visual's Fisher card cue chip

kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed page — 4 patterns (the 2-mean t-test stem, the 3-mean ANOVA stem, the 3-age-group proportions chi-square stem, the 20-and-20 small-sample Fisher stem), 4 traps (t-test vs ANOVA group count; means family vs chi-square's '(not mean values)' fence; chi-square vs Fisher sample size; the two printed 3-group examples colliding), 3 pivots (the tree router, the compared-quantity tell, the small-sample flip), and 8 recall cards covering all four rows plus the tree.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the four definitions and the figure only; the attack structure, distractor shapes, and question drills are KYP's design.
